acceptance_criteria.note: The PR's brief is the four findings of eval_R1-AI-FOUNDATION-AI.9_round_1.json. (1) Session-wide ceiling across service restarts: VERIFIED. AiBridge takes usage_from at the first launch (ai_bridge.gd:404-406), sums this session's lines by route (session_nusd, :309-318) and passes spent in every stub/live config (:289-291, live_plan reuses stub_config); spend.ledgerFrom starts the ledger from it (ai/spend.ail:83-84) and spentError refuses unknown providers and negatives (:85-90); service.ail:134 and :189 use ledgerFrom for both entries. test_session_ceiling (one process vs a fresh process per request, with an earlier session's 5.0 line) is green, its 4 mutants are killed, and my own probe reproduced it and showed a ceiling raise then lower keeps the carried spend (P5). (2) Interrupted calls charged: VERIFIED. adapters.ail:33-34,44,54,67 charge a std/net or std/ai Err after send at textCallCap/ttsCallCap; the loopback /drop endpoint proves both (172 and 6+98 tokens, usage lines d1/d12); provider.reservation + cache.reserveUsage write inflight.json before each live call (service.ail:177) and the bridge deletes it before each send (:466) and consumes it on timeout/fault only when it names the request and is provisional (:567-578); test_killed_charge covers timeout, fault, stale req, left-before-send and its 4 mutants are killed. (3) Guard hardened against the 5 evasions: VERIFIED (all five are mutants and caught; my re-run of the five on the new guard: caught). (4) Cheap gaps: VERIFIED (spaced/apostrophe key path, empty/blank key file, automation without indicator, earlier-session usage, digest over every ai/ and data/ai/ file, stale session key cleanup, scratch HOME for both smokes; 4 settings mutants killed). -6: (a) the carried spend is not bounded above and admit() overflows: a usage line with an absurd usd (1e300, or anything whose nano value exceeds int64) makes session_nusd saturate to 9223372036854775807, the service accepts it and total(l)+estimate wraps negative so every request is ADMITTED (reproduced through the bridge, probe P4/P4b, and directly against the service on both the VM and the interpreter with spent 9223372036854775807 and 9223372036854775000; spent 100 USD correctly refuses). The brief asked for a corrupted usage file to err safe; this corner errs open. Only the player can write such a line today, so it does not block an attended run, but it is a one-line clamp. (b) the new unpack-digest test is the CI breaker. (c) 11 of my 28 new guard probes survived (see adversarial_probes), three of them plausible spellings.

code_quality.note: LOC +636/-125 for four findings with self-proving mutants: proportionate. No TODO/HACK, no function over 50 lines, files under 800. -2 admit()/ledgerFrom have no upper bound (fail-open on overflow, see acceptance (a)); -1 test_live_env's new assertion `--ai-key-file keeps the spaced path whole` (tests/test_ai_bridge.gd:319) matches `ARGS $*`, which joins argv with spaces, so it cannot distinguish a split path from a whole one; the real protection is the `cat "$1"` mutant killed via the key value, so the assertion is decoration, not evidence; -1 test_unpack_digest depends on an untracked directory (runtime/) and so on `make runtime` having run, which CI never does; -1 the sprint JSON records nothing of the hardening (AI.9 notes unchanged; the design doc and changelog do). Noise: session_nusd calls JSON.parse_string on every line, which push_errors on any non-JSON line (seen in my P1 probe), so a corrupted file spams the log every launch; harmless but worth a JSON.new().parse.

documentation.note: changelogs/unreleased/2026-10-03-ai9-hardening.md: present, accurate, one bullet per item. Design doc gains 'AI.9 hardening' as-built (ceiling, interrupted calls, guard, smaller gaps, mutants, a note for AI.10b that the reservation is the worst case, not the bill). The args-json alias workaround is cited in ai/service.ail:43-44 and the upstream report exists (inbox user, from stapledons_godot, 'args-json: list of named record alias does not decode', AILANG v0.52.0 bf2436a). -1: the 'session' the ceiling bounds is one Godot run (usage_from is taken per AiBridge instance), so quitting and relaunching the game starts a fresh ceiling; true to D-20's 'a session' but worth one sentence for AI.10b's report, which should sum usage.ndjson over the whole run.

design_fidelity.note: Matches the brief and the design's (a5) intent: one ledger over both providers for the session, the indicator and the ledger now read the same lines, interrupted calls counted conservatively. All seven declared deviations judged acceptable (deviation_verdicts). -2: two places still lose or invert the 'never under-count' rule: (i) overflow admits everything (acceptance (a)); (ii) AiBridge.shutdown() with a live call in flight (game exit, AiSession._exit_tree) kills the service without _charge_interrupted, leaves inflight.json, and the next session's first _send_next deletes it unread, so that call's cost is recorded nowhere (probe P6/P6b). Not a ceiling bypass within a session, but the usage.ndjson record that AI.10b's cost report reads under-counts by up to one reservation per quit-mid-call.

evaluator_verifications.ceiling_carry_path: ai_bridge.gd:404-406 usage_from set once at the first _launch (file length, or 0); :309-318 session_nusd seeks there, parses each line, counts only route in {gemini, openrouter} with a numeric usd >= 0 (NaN and negatives dropped), roundi(usd*1e9); :324-326 spent_list -> config.spent for stub_config and live_plan alike; _charge_interrupted writes its provisional line BEFORE _failure schedules the relaunch (:546-549, :554-560), so the next launch's spent includes it. Service: start() validates spentError (service.ail:110), session/live use ledgerFrom. Confirmed by probe: restart per request gives the same 10:budget/11:budget as one process (baseline), and with garbage lines appended (P1).
evaluator_verifications.reservation_lifecycle: Written only in liveLoop's Run(j) branch (service.ail:177), i.e. for admitted cache-miss requests in a live process; never by the stub (killed_charge fakes it with a shell service, which is why the live reserveUsage call is 'untested' - see deviation_verdicts). Deleted by the bridge before every send (:466); after a successful result it stays on disk, stale, until the next send or kill. Consumed on _timeout and _fault only when req matches and provisional == true (:572-573); 'stale req' and 'left before send' cases proven. writeFile is truncate+write, not atomic, but the bridge only reads it 30-120 s later (timeout) or on a fault, so a torn read is theoretical.
evaluator_verifications.double_count_direction: A faulted request is re-queued (:556-557) and resent to a process whose spent includes the provisional line: counted twice when the resend succeeds (declared; errs safe). A timeout kill is async (OS.kill on the worker pool, :616-621) so a service finishing at that instant may also append its real line: also double, errs safe. The one under-count race: _charge_interrupted appends with READ_WRITE + seek_end + store_string (no O_APPEND) while a still-alive service may append; a torn line would then be dropped from the sum. Needs the service to finish its HTTP call in the microseconds between seek_end and the write; accepted as theoretical.
evaluator_verifications.settings_change_mid_call: AiSession.settings_changed() applies the new ceiling to the bridge at once (ai_settings.gd:189-195) but shuts the service down only when bridge.pending() == 0 (ai_session.gd:72-74), so a running call finishes under the old ceiling and the relaunch starts from the carried spend (probe P5). No mid-call reset path found.
evaluator_verifications.interpreter_vm_parity_of_overflow: The overflow admission reproduces identically on --bytecode and the interpreter (no parity bug, just int64 wraparound in total(l) + estimate <= l.ceiling).
evaluator_verifications.args_json_workaround: Same-module alias [Spent] decodes fine on v0.52.0 (my minimal repro); the failing case is an imported alias inside a list, as the upstream message says. Spelling the record out in Session (service.ail:45) is the right local workaround and the citation is at the site.

ceiling.P1_corrupted_lines: appended 'not json', usd as a string, usd -1.0, usd null, a JSON array and an unterminated object: session sum unchanged (39000000/40420 nano), 10 and 11 still budget. NOTE: an unterminated last line glues the service's next usage line onto it (1 glued line), losing that line from the sum; only external corruption can produce one (service and bridge both end lines with \n).
ceiling.P2_truncate_to_zero_after_9: 10 ok (ceiling reset), 11 budget, 12 ok; usage_from=0 here because the file was created after the first launch, so later lines were still counted. If usage_from were past the new EOF, nothing later would ever count. Player-only; acceptable per brief, noted.
ceiling.P4_absurd_usd: a line with usd 1e300 (or 9.3e9 USD): session_nusd saturates at 9223372036854775807, spent passes spentError, and requests 3 and 4 are ADMITTED 'ok' instead of budget. Reproduced against the service directly on VM and interpreter with spent 9223372036854775807 and 9223372036854775000; spent 100 USD -> budget. FAIL-OPEN on overflow. Fix: bridge clamps a line's nusd (e.g. to 1e12 nano) or ignores lines above it; spend.spentError rejects nusd above a sane bound; admit compares estimate <= ceiling - total (saturating).
ceiling.P5_ceiling_raised_then_lowered: 10 budget at 0.05 -> raise to 0.06 -> 10 still budget (its estimate exceeds the headroom) -> lower to 0.05 -> 11 budget: the carried spend survives every relaunch.
ceiling.P6_shutdown_mid_call: shutdown() with a reserved call in flight: inflight.json left, no usage line written, pending() still 1; a new bridge's first send deletes the stale reservation unread (P6b). The interrupted call is recorded nowhere. Fix: shutdown() calls _charge_interrupted(_in_flight) when live.
ceiling.P7_foreign_route: a provisional line with route 'openai' is appended but not summed and the config spent stays valid (service would not refuse).

deviation_verdicts.sim_exception_in_the_guard: ACCEPT with a narrowing requested. The sim's own run lines legitimately use a variable entry with --package-dir sim and the sim has no live entry, so some exception is needed. But the exception keys on the literal '--package-dir sim' and the absence of two spellings of the ai package, not on what program is run: three of my probes launch a service file through it (see survived_11). Require the program path on the line to be a literal under sim/.

deviation_verdicts.provisional_line_on_mid_call_fault_too: ACCEPT. A fault (child_eof, bad_response) with a reserved call in flight is exactly a process that may have been billed; the request is also resent, so the worst case is counted twice (reservation plus actual). Conservative, as the design doc says.

deviation_verdicts.std_ai_step_err_charged_at_cap: ACCEPT. std/ai returns one Err for pre-send failures (auth, DNS) and post-send ones alike, so the adapter cannot tell them apart; charging the cap errs safe and the ceiling is small. Cost: an unreachable provider burns the ceiling in refusals at ~1 cap per attempt, which is the right failure mode for an attended run.

Add a loopback lane that drives liveLoop over stdin against the fake server, then a mutant removing the reserveUsage call.

verdict_for_attended_live_run: SAFE IN SUBSTANCE for AI.10b with a low --ceiling-usd, once CI is green. Why: the ceiling now survives every service restart (verified by the suite and by my own restart-per-request, raise-then-lower and corrupted-file probes), interrupted calls are counted at their worst case through both the adapter (transport Err) and the bridge (timeout/fault reservation), the indicator and the ledger read the same lines, and every live launch still goes through the env -i wrapper with --ai-no-adc and key files. The remaining holes need the player to hand-edit usage.ndjson (truncate, delete, or write an absurd usd - the last one fails OPEN and must be clamped before any player-facing release), or a quit mid-call (one reservation unrecorded). The guard evasions I found are spellings an agent would have to write into make/tests/tools deliberately; none is reachable by the attended run itself. Worst-case attended exposure is ~ceiling + one request's worst case (a lowered ceiling takes effect after the running call) plus any call interrupted by quitting the game. Watch the indicator; sum usage.ndjson for the report.
